title: FX Brief — 13 Nov 2026
intro: Asian session trading on Friday, November 13, 2026, exhibits a risk-off tone as equity markets digest Nvidia's ongoing struggles and a widespread Microsoft outage. The US dollar maintains a firm bid supported by rising Treasury yields, with the US 10-year yield surging 10.5 basis points to 5.103 percent.

sections.heading: FX theme
sections.content: Rising US bond yields and severe tech sector headwinds dominate the session, placing significant downward pressure on high-beta commodity currencies. Meanwhile, safe-haven demand supports the US dollar and Japanese yen while risk assets like the S&P 500 retreat 0.35 percent.

sections.heading: Dollar read
sections.content: The DXY trades at 103.14 with a strong weekly gain of 1.5 percent, bolstered by US 10-year yields jumping 24.4 basis points over the week to 5.103 percent. Commodity currencies suffer notably, led by AUD/USD dropping 0.71 percent to 0.6794 amid the broader risk-off environment.

sections.heading: Crosses
sections.content: Yen crosses are broadly weaker as AUD/JPY drops 0.69 percent to 108.539 and EUR/JPY slips 0.26 percent to 176.757, reflecting defensive positioning. Euro crosses show mixed performance with EUR/AUD gaining 0.43 percent to 1.6284 as the Australian dollar underperforms.

sections.heading: Potential scenarios
sections.content:
- *▼ Bearish · EUR/USD — below 1.1050 opens 1.0950 · invalid above 1.1120*
Persistent US yield strength and negative euro area sentiment push the pair lower.
- *▲ Bullish · USD/JPY — above 160.000 opens 162.500 · invalid below 158.500*
Widening yield differentials and strong US 10-year rates at 5.103 percent support dollar strength against the yen.
- *▼ Bearish · AUD/USD — below 0.6780 opens 0.6650 · invalid above 0.6860*
Weaker commodity currency sentiment and risk aversion weigh heavily on the Australian dollar.
- *▲ Bullish · USD/CAD — above 1.4280 opens 1.4450 · invalid below 1.4150*
Broad US dollar buying and firm rate expectations lift the pair above recent resistance.

sections.heading: Key risks
sections.content:
- Upcoming US PPI and Core PPI data releases at 14:30 CET may trigger increased volatility across rates and the US dollar.
- Ongoing fallout from major tech sector disruptions and equity market weakness could accelerate safe-haven flows.
